new.s: What is meant by a 'debt trap'?
o: Borrowing to pay interest on past debt
Repaying debt out of a revenue surplus
new.x: A debt trap arises when a government borrows just to pay interest on its past debt, so debt keeps growing.

new.s: Which was the largest component of India's external debt at end-December 2025?
new.x: Commercial borrowings have long been the largest component of India's external debt and were still the largest at end-December 2025.

new.s: Provident Fund is an example of which type of savings?
new.x: Provident Fund is contractual savings: a fixed part of salary is saved under a contract. It is an 'other liability' of the Centre.
new.angle: U0547 notes gap: PF = contractual savings

new.s: In which year did the Centre's debt-GDP ratio reach its peak of about 61%?
new.x: Central debt peaked at about 61% of GDP in the pandemic year 2020-21; it is 55.6% in BE 2026-27.

new.s: Which consequence of deficit financing refers to borrowing merely to pay interest on past loans?
new.x: A debt trap is borrowing to pay interest on old loans; it leaves little money for health and education.

new.s: What is the effect of deficit financing through borrowing from the RBI on the money supply?
o: It leaves the money supply unchanged
It turns the money supply into foreign exchange
new.x: When the RBI lends to the government it creates new money, so money supply rises; that is why deficit financing is inflationary.
new.angle: U0548 #1/#6 APPSC PYQ y25b2c47a482 angle: inflationary character

new.s: On 15 September 2026, the RBI announced open market operation (OMO) sales of how much?
new.x: On 15 September 2026 the RBI announced OMO sales of ₹1 lakh crore; an OMO sale drains liquidity.
new.angle: U0548 #5 notes gap: OMO sales Sep 2026

new.s: Which deficit shows the total borrowing requirement of the government?
new.x: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts; it equals the total borrowing requirement.
new.angle: U0549 #1/#16 FD meaning (APPSC PYQ ydf45fd20217, yc7a4faba756)

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts.
2. Revenue deficit is revenue receipts minus revenue expenditure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is the fiscal deficit formula. Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts, not the other way round.

new.s: Which of the following is an instrument of monetary policy and not of fiscal policy?
new.x: The repo rate is set by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee; taxation, spending and borrowing are fiscal tools.

new.s: What is it called when public capital expenditure draws in more private investment?
new.x: Crowding in is when public capex attracts private investment; crowding out is when government borrowing pushes it out.
new.angle: U0549 #6/#14 Crowding out vs crowding in

new.s: In which type of budget is every item justified afresh, with no base taken from the previous year?
new.x: In zero-based budgeting every item starts from zero and must be justified again each period.

new.s: Which of the following is a non-developmental expenditure?
new.x: Interest, defence and administration are non-developmental; education, health and roads are developmental.

new.s: Who is the author of 'The General Theory' (1936), which made fiscal policy a tool against depression?
new.x: J.M. Keynes wrote the General Theory in 1936 and argued for active demand management through fiscal policy.

new.s: In which year was India's Long-Term Fiscal Policy laid in Parliament?
new.x: Finance Minister V.P. Singh laid the Long-Term Fiscal Policy in Parliament on 19 December 1985.

new.s: From which Latin word is the word 'fiscal' derived?
new.x: 'Fiscal' comes from the Latin 'fiscus', meaning a basket or the public purse.

new.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Progressive taxation helps reduce inequality of income.
Reason (R): Under progressive taxation, the tax rate rises as income rises.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
new.x: Because richer people pay a higher rate, progressive taxation takes more from the rich; this is the distribution function of fiscal policy.
new.angle: U0549 #5/#9 APPSC PYQ yeecdd655235 angle: assertion on tax policy effect

new.s: Total subsidies form about what share of Union expenditure in 2026-27?
new.x: Food, fertiliser and petroleum subsidies together form about 8.5% of Union expenditure in 2026-27.
new.angle: U0549 #11 APPSC PYQ y476e4314539 angle: subsidy share data

new.s: Under the new FRBM framework of 2018, which target was dropped?
new.x: The 2018 amendment made debt the anchor with fiscal deficit as the operational target, and dropped the revenue deficit targets.

new.s: What is a double-dip recession?
o: A recession, a short recovery and then another recession
Two consecutive quarters of falling GDP
A recession in two countries at the same time
new.x: A double-dip recession is a recession followed by a short recovery and then another recession.

new.s: How many sovereign rating upgrades did India get in 2025 after cutting its fiscal deficit from 9.2% to 4.4% of GDP?
new.x: Fiscal consolidation brought three rating upgrades in 2025, from Morningstar DBRS, S&P and R&I.

new.s: N.K. Singh headed which of the following?
o: Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act (2004)
new.x: N.K. Singh chaired the FRBM Review Committee of 2016; Vijay Kelkar chaired the 2004 Task Force and the 13th Finance Commission.
new.angle: U0550 #9 Review Committee -> chairman (APPSC PYQ y95295561528)

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: N.K. Singh – Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act
Yashwant Sinha – Introduced the FRBM Act
Urjit Patel – Chairman of the FRBM Review Committee
new.x: Yashwant Sinha introduced the FRBM Act. N.K. Singh chaired the Review Committee (Urjit Patel was a member) and Kelkar chaired the 2004 Task Force.

new.s: In which year did the N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee submit its report?
new.x: The committee was formed in May 2016 and gave its report in January 2017; it was reflected in Budget 2017-18.

new.s: Up to which year did the N.K. Singh Committee recommend keeping the fiscal deficit at 3% of GDP?
new.x: It recommended a 3% fiscal deficit for three years up to 2019-20, then 2.5% by 2022-23.
new.angle: U0550 #9 APPSC PYQ yefdb37dcb26 angle: N.K. Singh deficit target

new.s: Which of the following is NOT laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act?
new.x: The Annual Financial Statement is laid under Article 112 of the Constitution; the other three are FRBM statements.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2018 amendment to the FRBM Act:
1. It made debt the anchor of fiscal policy.
2. It retained the target of eliminating the revenue deficit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 2018 amendment set a debt anchor (general government 60%, Centre 40%) and dropped the revenue deficit targets.

new.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's fiscal deficit as a share of GSDP in its Budget Estimates 2026-27?
new.x: AP's BE 2026-27 puts the fiscal deficit at 3.84% of GSDP, above the 3% norm; 4.57% was the 2025-26 RE.
new.angle: U0550 #4/#12 notes gap: AP FD BE 2026-27

new.s: Which of the following is a criticism of the working of the FRBM Act?
o: No fiscal council has been set up yet
It applies automatically to all States
It lets the RBI fix the fiscal deficit
new.x: Critics point to frequent use of the escape clause, deferrals, no penalty and no fiscal council yet.

new.s: Which of the following gives the revenue deficit?
new.x: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts; fiscal deficit minus interest is the primary deficit.
new.angle: U0551 APPSC PYQ ydbb3d3a7026 angle: RD formula

new.s: Which practice of 92 years ended with the Union Budget 2017-18?
new.x: The separate Railway Budget, begun in 1924, was merged with the General Budget in 2017-18.

new.s: Who presented the first budget of independent India on 26 November 1947?
new.x: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented independent India's first budget; Liaquat Ali Khan presented the Interim Government budget.
new.angle: U0551 #3/#13 First budget (APPSC PYQ y98a3def9930 presenter angle)

new.s: Who shifted the time of presenting the Union Budget from 5 pm to 11 am in 2001?
new.x: Finance Minister Yashwant Sinha moved the Budget time from 5 pm to 11 am in 2001.

new.s: Which of the following was a non-plan expenditure item?
new.x: Interest payments were the classic and largest non-plan item; the others were plan expenditure.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a Department of the Ministry of Finance?
new.x: Economic Affairs, Revenue and Expenditure are Departments of the Ministry of Finance; the Banking Division is not.

new.s: Under which Ministry is PM-DevINE, announced in Budget 2022-23, a central sector scheme?
o: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
new.x: PM-DevINE is a central sector scheme under DoNER for infrastructure and livelihoods in the North-East.

new.s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Purvodaya plan of Budget 2024-25?
new.x: Purvodaya covers Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, not Gujarat.

new.s: Which body first recommended performance budgeting in the USA in 1949?
new.x: Performance budgeting came from the USA on the First Hoover Commission (1949); India took it up from the late 1960s on ARC advice.
new.angle: U0551 #4 notes gap: performance budget origin

new.s: What is the total expenditure in the Union Budget 2026-27?
new.x: Budget 2026-27 puts total expenditure (equal to total receipts) at ₹53,47,315 crore, up 7.7%.

new.s: What is the disinvestment target in the Union Budget 2026-27?
new.x: Budget 2026-27 sets a disinvestment target of ₹80,000 crore; disinvestment is a non-debt capital receipt.

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with supplementary, additional or excess grants?
new.x: Article 115 covers supplementary, additional or excess grants; Article 116 covers vote on account.

new.s: Which Union Budget is known as the 'Black Budget'?
new.x: The 1973-74 Budget is called the 'Black Budget'; 1997-98 is the 'Dream Budget'.

new.s: In which Economic Survey was 'pious obligation' to repay debts put forward as a guiding principle?
new.x: The Economic Survey 2018-19 (4 July 2019), built on behavioural economics, spoke of a 'pious obligation' to repay debts.

new.s: In which year did the Centre's gross tax revenue record its highest growth, of 17.9%?
new.x: Gross tax revenue growth was highest in 2016-17 (17.9%), against 16.9% in 2015-16 and 11.8% in 2017-18.
new.angle: U0552 #2 APPSC PYQ ya095c14018a angle: tax revenue data

new.s: Where is the headquarters of UN ESCAP, which brings out its own Economic Survey of Asia and the Pacific?
new.x: UN ESCAP is headquartered in Bangkok; its survey is separate from India's Economic Survey.

new.s: What is the title of Chapter 1 of the Economic Survey 2025-26?
o: State of the Economy: Pushing the Growth Frontier
new.x: Chapter 1 is 'State of the Economy: Pushing the Growth Frontier'; 'Building Strategic Indispensability' is the Survey's theme.
